question: Do Palmer Adelie breeding groups that subsequently undergo durable colony-code extinction already show depressed chick production in the immediately preceding breeding season, after conditioning on their breeding-pair abundance and shared island-year reproductive conditions?

biological_hypothesis.name: pre-extinction reproductive-performance syndrome
biological_hypothesis.prediction: Within the same island and breeding season, colony codes that will be durably absent at the next breeding census produce fewer creched chicks than expected from their current breeding-pair abundance.
biological_hypothesis.mechanistic_role: This tests an upstream local-state signal before the stochastic zero boundary. It does not assume that one season of low chick production causes next-year disappearance, because recruits enter the breeding population years later.

adult_census.role: frozen durable-extinction labels, prior breeding-pair counts and island-year risk sets

newer_reference.role: provenance/update target; do not silently mix revisions in the primary analysis

season_alignment.hazard_transition: adult breeding-pair census at season t -> adult breeding-pair census at season t+1
season_alignment.chick_timing: January chick count from breeding season t, after the adult census at t and before the adult census at t+1

chick_data_cleaning.primary_uses: Chicks only; the Adults field in the chick table is not used as the denominator or size predictor.
chick_data_cleaning.duplicate_rule: For an island-colony-season key with multiple records, retain a single chick count only if all finite chick counts are exactly identical; otherwise exclude that key as ambiguous.
chick_data_cleaning.reason_for_external_adult_size: Use the already-frozen November breeding-pair census for size so the test does not inherit duplicate or zero Adult fields from the January chick table.

eligibility.base: Use the parent hazard primary transitions and durable-extinction definition without alteration.
eligibility.joined_row: Exact island + colony_code + season_start_year match to a unique cleaned chick count.
eligibility.risk_set: At least one durable-extinction event and at least one non-event with joined chick data in the same island-year; at least 2 joined colonies total.

size_conditioned_reproductive_null.within_each_risk_set: Condition on the observed total chicks C across joined at-risk colony codes.
size_conditioned_reproductive_null.equal_per_pair_productivity: Expected allocation probability p_j = prior_breeding_pairs_j / sum prior_breeding_pairs over joined colonies.
size_conditioned_reproductive_null.sampling_null: Draw chick counts jointly as Multinomial(C, p).
size_conditioned_reproductive_null.interpretation: Under the null, every breeding pair has the same expected contribution to chick production within that island-season; differences arise only from finite count allocation.

primary_statistic.risk_set_contrast: mean r_j among durable-extinction events minus mean r_j among non-events.

inference.procedure: For every simulation, independently draw a multinomial chick allocation within every informative risk set using the frozen size-conditioned null, recompute the same equal-weight cross-risk-set statistic, and compare with the observed statistic.
inference.p_value: one-sided lower-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

secondary_outputs: number of matched colony-season rows, informative risk sets and matched durable-extinction events
event and non-event mean/median observed chicks
event and non-event mean Pearson performance residual
leave-one-island-out primary contrast and p value when estimable
same test excluding risk sets with total chicks < 10
same test using deviance residuals from the proportional multinomial expectation as a descriptive sensitivity

decision_rule.support: Observed cross-risk-set reproductive-performance contrast < 0 and one-sided multinomial-null p <= 0.05.
decision_rule.strong: Support plus negative leave-one-island-out contrast for at least 4 of the 5 islands where estimable.
decision_rule.no_support: Otherwise do not claim a colony-level pre-extinction reproductive penalty.

interpretation_boundaries: A supported result would identify a local pre-extinction performance syndrome, not a causal effect of chick production on next-year adult occupancy.
Do not call low chick production an Allee effect without an independent nonlinear density test.
Do not attribute the syndrome specifically to snow, predation, food or disturbance without a separate predictor test.
The January chick census and November adult census share colony identifiers but are distinct life-stage observations; exact data provenance and duplicate exclusions must be reported.
The primary source revision is 88.8 because it is the accessible frozen snapshot. Revision 88.9 may be used only as a prespecified replication/update after the 88.8 primary result is frozen.
